claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me ask you the first question:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The child's age or date of birth
- Whether they are under 16, 16-19 years old, or 20 or over
- If you have multiple children, please provide the age(s) of each

This will help determine which eligibility path applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my daughter Alex. She's 9 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex. So Alex is 9 years old, which means she's under 16 - that's very helpful.

Let me continue with the assessment by moving to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is under 16, I can confirm she qualifies as a dependent child. However, I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Question 1: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is she not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 9 years old, I'd expect she's not in paid work, but I want to confirm this for the record.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not working at all - she's only 9, so she's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Alex is in primary school and not working, so she passes this check.

Let me move forward with the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 2: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in her own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking whether Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in her own right (as her own claim, not as a dependant on your claim)?

For a 9-year-old in primary school, the answer would typically be "yes" (meaning she's not receiving these benefits), but I want to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - she doesn't get any benefits in her own name. She's just a regular 9-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in her own right. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 3: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Again, this is quite straightforward for a 9-year-old in primary school, but I need to confirm: Is Alex currently undertaking any kind of apprenticeship programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - she's only 9 and in primary school, so no apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency situation, as this is an important eligibility requirement.

**Question 4: Do you (the claimant) meet UK residency requirements?**

There are several ways you might qualify. Do ANY of the following apply to you?

1. **Normally live in the UK** - You're based in the UK most of the time
2. **Settled status under EU Settlement Scheme** - You have settled status
3. **Pre-settled status under EU Settlement Scheme** - AND one of:
   - You're working and earning/expecting to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work as a jobseeker, OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support your family (and not claiming Income Support, JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit), OR
   - You're studying with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
4. **Crown servant abroad** - You're living abroad as a Crown servant in certain qualifying countries

For most people in the UK, the first option applies - you normally live in the UK. Is that your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I live in the UK. I'm based in Manchester, so I definitely normally live here.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check whether you're responsible for Alex.

**Question 5: Are you responsible for Alex?**

This can be satisfied in a few ways. Do ANY of the following apply?

1. **You live with Alex** - You share a home with her and she lives with you
2. **You contribute to her upkeep** - You pay toward her care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.) at least the amount equivalent to Child Benefit
3. **Maintenance payments** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement that covers her upkeep

You mentioned earlier that Alex "lives at home with you," so I believe the first option applies - you live with her. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex and she lives at home with you, so you're clearly responsible for her. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check an important question about other claimants.

**Question 6: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any dispute about who should be claiming?**

Specifically:
- Is Alex's other parent (or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for her?
- If so, have you agreed between you who should be claiming, or is there a dispute?

For context, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child, so if both parents are eligible, you need to agree on who will claim.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after her.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So there's no other claimant for Alex. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 7: Where is Alex currently living?**

I need to check if any special circumstances apply:

- Is Alex currently in hospital?
- Is she in care (residential care or similar)?
- Is she fostered?
- Or is she living normally at home with you?

Based on what you've told me, I believe she's living normally at home with you in Manchester, is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - she's living normally at home with me. No hospital, care, or fostering - just a regular home situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the final check.

**Question 8: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council paying for Alex's housing, food, care, or other maintenance?
- Or are you paying for all of this yourself?

For a typical family situation where the parent is supporting their child, the answer would be "yes" (the council is not paying). Is that the case for you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting her myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're supporting Alex yourself and the council isn't paying towards her accommodation or maintenance. Let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I have all the information I need to give you your eligibility assessment.

conversation.text:
## ✅ **Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit**

**For: Alex (age 9)**

### Summary
You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. She is a qualifying child who lives with you, and you are responsible for her support.

### Why You're Eligible
- ✓ Alex is under 16 years old
- ✓ She is not working
- ✓ She is not receiving benefits in her own right
- ✓ She is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✓ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✓ You live with Alex and are responsible for her
- ✓ No other person is claiming for her
- ✓ She is living normally at home
- ✓ The council is not paying towards her support

### Next Steps - How to Claim

You can now apply for Child Benefit:

1. **Apply online** at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
2. **Or apply by post** using form CH2

### What You'll Need to Provide
- Proof of your identity
- Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
- Child's National Insurance number (if you have it)

### Important Information

**High Income Child Benefit Charge:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which means you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through self-assessment tax returns. The charge applies at increasing rates as income rises above this threshold.

**Payment Frequency:** Child Benefit is normally paid every 4 weeks. However, if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits, you can request weekly payments.

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations, and best of luck with your claim!

She meets all Child Benefit eligibility requirements.
